title: 12 Weeks of Cosmetic Light on Redness and Blemishes
official: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Consumer Perception of a Cosmetic Light Device on Redness and Blemishes and Obtain Images
summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy and perception a commercial LED device in 168 healthy adult females and males between the ages of 18-65 years old, inclusively. The main questions it aims to answer are: Does daily use of this commercial LED device improve objective measures of skin health (expert clinical grading, cutometer, digital photography, and VISIA-CR? Does daily use of this commercial LED device improve subjective skin appearance? Is daily use of this commercial LED device well tolerated? Does daily use of this commercial LED device set to an acne-specific setting improve blemishes? Participants assigned to the redness/rejuvenation group will complete a 9-minute light treatment (3 minutes of each red light, red+infrared light, yellow light); while those assigned to the blemishes/acne group will complete a 9-minute light treatment (3 minutes of each: blue light, red light, yellow light) with a commercially available device every day for 12 weeks. Participants will be divided into two groups: blemish and rejuvenation/redness. Participants will be asked to attend the clinic at various time points throughout the study to get clinical assessment of skin health. These are the primary outcomes of interest.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18-65
* All sexes and all ethnicities eligible
* Fitzpatrick Skin Types I-VI, with a minimum of 2 subjects per type
* Willing to complete a 14-day washout period using only a bland cleanser (no active skincare or moisturizer with actives)
* Willing to avoid other facial treatments, devices, or professional skin procedures during the study period
* No use of at-home LED, microcurrent, or other skincare devices in the past 6 months

Additional Inclusion Criteria for Group 1 (Redness / Rejuvenation):

* At least 50% of Group 1 participants must present with visible baseline redness/erythema (score of 3 or higher on a 0-10 expert grading scale; exact scale and threshold to be finalized with research partner)
* Remaining participants may qualify via self-perceived uneven skin tone or general rejuvenation-focused concerns (cosmetic, non-diagnosed) Presence of wrinkles and fine lines (a score of 3 or higher)

Additional Inclusion Criteria for Group 2 (Breakout / Blemish):

* Self-reported history of occasional or recurring blemishes/breakouts
* Minimum of 5-20 visible non-cystic, non-nodular blemishes/comedones at baseline (exact count to be finalized with research partner)
* Not currently using prescription acne treatment

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosed dermatological condition (e.g., rosacea, eczema, psoriasis, cystic or nodular acne)
* Current or recent (within 3-6 months) use of prescription topical or oral acne treatment (retinoids, antibiotics, isotretinoin)
* Routine use of chemical peels or other professional facial skin treatments
* Botox within the last 3 months; filler within the last 6 months, including lip filler
* Topical or systemic medication within 14 days of study entry
* Pregnant or nursing
* Testing firms/laboratories, cosmetic or raw goods manufacturers or suppliers
* Participation in another anti-aging or facial skincare clinical study within the past 6 months
